meta.title: Matrix pencil: extracting damped exponentials from a transient
meta.tools: Hua–Sarkar matrix pencil (Hankel matrices, SVD rank truncation, generalised eigenvalues), least-squares amplitudes, comparison with FFT peak picking
meta.summary: Estimate the frequencies and damping factors of three closely spaced damped sinusoids in a noisy ringing transient with the matrix pencil method, show that it resolves modes an FFT cannot, and measure estimation error versus SNR.
meta.problem: A ringing circuit's transient is a sum of damped exponentials. How do you recover each mode's frequency and decay, even when they overlap spectrally?
meta.theory:
$x[n]=\sum_k c_kz_k^n$ with $z_k=e^{(-σ_k+jω_k)T}$. Hankel matrices Y₀ (rows 0…N−L−1) and Y₁ (shifted by one) satisfy Y₁ = Y₀·(something with eigenvalues z_k): the z_k are the non-zero eigenvalues of the pencil
$Y_0^+Y_1$ after truncating to the signal rank (2K for real signals). No frequency grid, so modes closer than the FFT's 1/T resolution are separable; errors grow as noise increases, approaching the Cramér–Rao
bound for moderate SNR.
meta.method:
fs = 1 MHz, N = 200 (T = 200 µs, FFT resolution 5 kHz). Modes: 100 kHz (σ = 5000 s⁻¹), 103 kHz (σ = 8000), 150 kHz (σ = 20000). SNR 10–60 dB, 100 trials each; pencil parameter L = N/3;
rank 6. Errors in frequency and damping.
